criteria_results.title: Identifies petition deadline of October 24, 2024 (20 days from service)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the 15 U.S.C. § 1314(b) petition deadline is Thursday, October 24, 2024, 20 days after the October 4 service.

criteria_results.title: Flags urgency: only 9 days remain from October 15 memo date to petition deadline
criteria_results.reasoning: The Oct. 24 deadline is bolded in the executive summary. The 72-hour action list requires contacting DOJ by Oct. 18 to address the petition deadline in writing and preparing a protective petition in parallel, so the short window is treated as needing immediate action.

criteria_results.title: Identifies overbreadth of DMD Specification 3 (pricing documents)
criteria_results.reasoning: Spec. 3 is called the largest cost driver (hundreds of thousands of hits, ~1.2M documents overall), with the 'to the present' period and the product-definition breadth also noted. The memo proposes narrowing it.

criteria_results.title: Recommends Specification 3 overbreadth as grounds for petition to modify
criteria_results.reasoning: Overbreadth of Spec. 3 and the other specs is tied to modification: a negotiated modification letter, with a protective § 1314(b) petition stating each ground as the fallback.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Hollister-Felding June 14, 2022 text as critical substantive risk
criteria_results.reasoning: Entry 23 (June 14, 2022, 'move prices up in July... You seeing the same thing?') is shown as the key pre-increase message before the July 1 increase and is treated as central per se Section 1 exposure.

criteria_results.title: Notes Hollister-Felding communications are largely personal and not privileged
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo says the CEO-to-CEO communications are not privileged and acknowledges the genuine personal content and the personal/business/mixed split.

criteria_results.title: Identifies failure to issue litigation hold as critical issue
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states that no litigation hold has issued 12 days after service, calls this the most time-sensitive issue, and says a hold must issue today.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Slack 90-day auto-deletion as spoliation risk
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo says the Slack 90-day purge destroyed nearly all 2022-2023 content and that it must be disclosed. It flags spoliation risk if the preservation trigger came earlier.

criteria_results.title: Recommends immediate issuance of litigation hold
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo says to 'Issue a written litigation hold today.'

criteria_results.title: Identifies March 15, 2024 server failure as data loss relevant to CID
criteria_results.reasoning: The March 15, 2024 Raleigh server failure (about two weeks of backup lost) is identified and tied to Interrogatory 8(f) disclosure.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Ridgeline report as likely not privileged
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo concludes the Ridgeline report is neither privileged nor work product, because it had a business purpose and the GC's role was vendor-contract management.

criteria_results.title: Notes Ridgeline engagement letter lacks legal purpose or at-direction-of-counsel language
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo notes the engagement letter states a business purpose, that Ridgeline is 'not a legal representative', and that Ridgeline was not assisting counsel in giving legal advice, which is the substance of the missing counsel-direction language.

criteria_results.title: Identifies damaging content in Ridgeline report (±3% price parity recommendation)
criteria_results.reasoning: The ±3% price-parity corridor with TinyHarvest (NourishCo's brand) is identified as damaging content.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Ridgeline report as responsive to DMD Specification 11
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the report and related materials are responsive to Spec. 11 and must be produced.

criteria_results.title: Discusses Kovel doctrine or third-party consultant privilege requirements
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo discusses Kovel and explains why it does not apply, along with the primary-purpose test from Kellogg Brown & Root.

criteria_results.title: Identifies common interest agreement scope limitation to labeling litigation
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the CIA covers only counsel-to-counsel communications on defense of the Labeling Litigation, and that pricing and competitive-dynamics exchanges fall outside that scope.

criteria_results.title: Identifies absence of termination clause in common interest agreement
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo acknowledges there is no termination clause, notes the § 5 withdrawal right, and addresses the survival of protection for materials shared before settlement.

criteria_results.title: Analyzes whether common interest privilege survived settlement of labeling litigation
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo analyzes that the common legal interest ended with the April 30, 2023 settlement and that communications after that date are not protected.

criteria_results.title: Identifies CID signature authority issue (delegation from AAG)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies the CID as signed by a Senior Trial Attorney 'by authority of' the AAG under § 1312(a) and recommends confirming the delegation.

criteria_results.title: Correctly characterizes signature authority issue as weak or secondary ground
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo characterizes the delegation point as unlikely to help and as an objection to preserve rather than lead with.

criteria_results.title: Identifies email migration data loss (~14,800 emails, 4%)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies ~14,800 of ~370,000 messages (4%) failing to migrate because of formatting and corruption errors.

criteria_results.title: Identifies obligation to disclose migration data gap to DOJ
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the data losses must be disclosed under Interrogatory 8, Instructions 4 and 8, and Topic D, and recommends proactive disclosure.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Google Workspace decommissioning as complicating recovery of unmigrated emails
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo notes the Oct. 1, 2023 decommissioning against Cloudbridge's advice made the emails unrecoverable and recovery unlikely.

criteria_results.title: Recommends engaging vendor to attempt recovery of unmigrated emails
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo recommends an immediate, documented recovery request to Google, obtaining Cloudbridge's failure logs, and identifying alternative sources, so a recovery effort is recommended.

criteria_results.title: Identifies oral testimony scheduling conflict (Nov 22 vs. Nov 18 return date)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags that testimony four days after the Nov. 18 return date leaves no time to prepare on the produced record.

criteria_results.title: Recommends requesting modification of oral testimony date
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo recommends seeking postponement of the testimony until after substantial production.

criteria_results.title: Identifies OINTA Pricing Index Database as potential collusion-facilitating mechanism
criteria_results.reasoning: The OINTA Pricing Index is analyzed as an information-exchange risk based on actual transaction prices, the lag, high/low values and summit discussion.

criteria_results.title: Discusses legal framework for competitor information exchanges via trade associations
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo cites Container Corp., Gypsum and Todd v. Exxon, discusses the withdrawn DOJ/FTC safety zones, and covers the data-age and aggregation factors.

criteria_results.title: Identifies need to collect from personal devices for Hollister-Felding communications
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo identifies the personal iPhone and Gmail sources and recommends forensic collection through an independent vendor.

criteria_results.title: Notes CID obligations extend to documents in company's possession, custody, or control including personal devices
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the communications are within the Company's possession, custody or control and that the CID expressly reaches personal devices used for business.

criteria_results.title: Does not flag parallel pricing alone as evidence of antitrust violation
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states that parallel price movement alone is lawful conscious parallelism under Twombly and relies on the communications as plus factors.
